name: Leucobryaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Leucobryum albidum as a compact pale cushion moss whose broad costa dominates most of the leaf and contains large hyaline leucocysts surrounding a central chlorocyst layer.

project_scope.note: Leucobryum albidum is accepted in the current WFO/FNA backbone and FNA includes Texas in its range.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Start with the pale cushion, then remove one leaf. In Leucobryum most of what looks like the leaf blade is actually a very broad costa.
family_diagnostics.gametophyte: Small to medium acrocarpous moss forming compact whitish-green cushions or turfs. Leaves crowded, with a sheathing base and a narrow concave to subtubulose limb.
family_diagnostics.leaf_anatomy: Costa extremely broad, built from large transparent leucocysts on both sides of a central layer of green chlorocysts. The ordinary lamina is reduced to only a narrow strip of cells.
family_diagnostics.sporophyte: Seta supports an inclined to curved capsule; in L. albidum the mature dry capsule is reddish to reddish brown and often strongly curved.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Whitish cushion + leaf dominated by a thick pale costa + leucocyst/chlorocyst sandwich in cross-section = Leucobryaceae/Leucobryum.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole cushion → single leaf → broad costa → cross-section leucocysts/chlorocysts → capsule → Pottiaceae/Leucodontaceae comparison
visual_lesson.intro: White moss looks pale because much of each leaf is built from large clear water-holding cells surrounding a thin green photosynthetic layer.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the pale cushion
steps.look_for: Low compact whitish-green cushions, usually only a few centimeters across.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the field gestalt before microscopy.

steps.title: 2 · Realize the costa is almost the whole leaf
steps.look_for: Broad pale costa occupying most of the leaf width; only a very narrow true lamina remains at the margins.
steps.why_it_matters: Corrects the assumption that the pale central area is just a normal midrib.

steps.title: 3 · Cut across the costa
steps.look_for: Large hyaline leucocysts above and below a central layer of smaller green chlorocysts.
steps.why_it_matters: This cell sandwich explains the family appearance and is the strongest teaching structure.

steps.title: 4 · Separate albidum from larger white-moss lookalikes
steps.look_for: Small low cushions; leaves usually 2–4 mm, with the narrow limb shorter than the expanded sheath.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA emphasizes the small plant and short limb as useful L. albidum clues.

steps.title: 5 · Find the curved red-brown capsule
steps.look_for: Inclined capsule becoming strongly curved when dry and empty, red to reddish brown.
steps.why_it_matters: Adds reproductive confirmation to the cushion/leaf lesson.

comparisons.title: Leucobryaceae vs Pottiaceae
comparisons.rule: Leucobryum has a leaf dominated by a broad multilayered leucocyst-rich costa and forms pale cushions. The project Pottiaceae concept has ordinary-looking green leaves with a strong costa, papillose upper cells, and strongly crisp/squarrose leaves.

comparisons.title: Leucobryaceae vs Leucodontaceae
comparisons.rule: Leucobryum is an upright cushion-forming acrocarp with pale thick leaves; Leucodon is a creeping/pleurocarpous bark-rock moss with cylindrical julaceous branches and leaves lacking a costa.

visual_lesson.caveat: Cushion color alone is not enough. The broad leucocyst-rich costa and cross-section anatomy are the dependable family-level structures.

genera.fast_cue: pale compact cushion + broad leucocyst-rich costa + narrow lamina

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted in current WFO/FNA; FNA distribution includes Texas.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label upper leucocysts, central chlorocysts and lower leucocysts
outline costa occupying most of leaf and true lamina at margins
label seta, capsule and dry curvature
